description: Illustrative operating relationships between the modeled roles. SaaS-to-commerce sales are examples, not universal claims about every merchant. Sellers are represented separately from direct merchant buyers; treasury and risk responsibilities remain with the named business.

relationTypes.name: Commercial
relationTypes.description: Contracting of subscriptions, platform participation, and services

relationTypes.name: Operational
relationTypes.description: Onboarding, KYC, and day-to-day money-movement operations

relationTypes.name: Financial
relationTypes.description: Invoicing, payouts, and settlement of funds between parties

relationTypes.name: Information
relationTypes.description: Usage events, dispute outcomes, and risk signals

relations.name: Contracts commerce teams on subscription plans
relations.description: Illustrative relationship: Sells commerce and operations software on recurring plans with usage-based tiers, negotiating packaging and pricing changes that must ship without an engineering rebuild.

relations.name: Pays recurring invoices
relations.description: Illustrative relationship: Settles subscription and metered invoices by card and bank debit; failed payments enter smart retries and dunning so the SaaS vendor recovers revenue instead of churning the account.

relations.name: Feeds usage events for metered billing
relations.description: Illustrative relationship: Streams consumption and seat-usage events that drive the SaaS vendor's usage-based invoices, keeping metered charges and month-end revenue recognition accurate.

relations.name: Onboards onto the platform as a seller
relations.description: Joins the platform as a connected account to reach its buyers, completing KYC/KYB identity verification and payout setup during platform onboarding.

relations.name: Splits and pays out platform sales
relations.description: Routes buyer funds across parties, deducts the platform's take rate and fees, and pays sellers out on schedule with reconcilable statements.

relations.name: Shares dispute and risk signals
relations.description: Relays chargeback outcomes, fraud scores, and account-risk flags to sellers on the platform so they can tighten checkout flows and submit better dispute evidence.

relations.name: Sells revenue tooling to platform operators
relations.description: Illustrative relationship: Contracts platform businesses on subscriptions for billing, invoicing, and revenue-analytics tooling that the platform team runs alongside its own money-movement stack.

relations.name: Sells through the platform's checkout
relations.description: Lists offers and accepts orders through the platform's storefront and checkout, extending reach into markets and payment methods the commerce team has not built directly.

relations.name: Explains platform balances and payout obligations
relations.description: The platform provides obligations, reserves, fees and recipient status for treasury funding and control.

relations.name: Approves funding and resolves cash exceptions
relations.description: Treasury authorizes eligible funding and returns material settlement or payout differences to the platform owner.

relations.name: Supplies controlled billing and revenue records
relations.description: Revenue operations supplies invoice, usage adjustment and recognition evidence for the controller’s close.
